slice: The Apps panel's address bar completes what is typed, from the search engine
method: desktop patch 0021 + apps/macos extension command + CDP on the running Agents window + bun test + bun run typecheck
why: the address bar searches, so a browser's own behaviour is to complete the term. The workbench renderer cannot: a fetch to suggestqueries.google.com from the window fails with 'Failed to fetch' (CORS), which was measured directly through CDP before writing this.

change.extension: caret.browser.suggest asks https://suggestqueries.google.com/complete/search?client=firefox&q= from the extension host, which runs on Node and is not subject to CORS, and returns at most eight terms. A failure, a timeout (2s) or a reply of the wrong shape returns an empty list instead of throwing. The Firefox client is used because it answers with JSON; the Chrome client answers with a callback.
change.parsing: apps/macos/src/browser-search.ts holds parseSuggestionPayload and searchUrlFor, so the shape of the engine's reply is testable without the network.
change.desktop: the address bar debounces 180ms while the term is a search term, asks for the list, and renders it under the bar: ArrowDown/ArrowUp move the highlight, Enter opens the highlighted suggestion, Escape closes it, and a row answers to mousedown so the input's blur cannot close the list first. A late answer for an older term never replaces the current list. The page a browser tab hosts is a native view above the window DOM, so the list had to be given room: while it is open the tab is laid out below the list height, and closing it restores the full bounds. Without that the rows existed in the DOM and every one of them was painted behind the page.
change.keyboard: a chosen row is always a search (never a host to open) while typed text still follows the earlier rule - a scheme or a bare host is a URL, anything else is a search.

verified.live: CDP on the running window: typing 'cats' in the Apps panel's Browser tab produced the engine's eight terms (cats, catster, catsolute, catsmile cafe, catster by kingdomoftigers, catsonic livehouse, cats แปลว่า, catsaur); ArrowDown highlighted 'cats' and Enter opened https://www.google.com/search?q=cats with the list closed and the bar reading 'cats'
verified.unitTests: apps/macos/test/browser-search.test.ts: the engine's reply shape, the endpoint's client parameter, unreadable replies (empty body, other JSON shapes, non-string entries), blanks/duplicates/cap, and the search URL encoding. ide-native-workbench.test.ts pins the address-bar wiring in the 0021 patch text.
verified.patchAgreement: 0021 regenerated for its own two files only, digest updated, 24/24 patches apply from the pinned base and the produced tree equals the checkout
verified.suites: 726 pass / 0 fail across packages/omp-adapter, packages/relay, apps/host and apps/macos/test
verified.ci: node scripts/ci-validate.mjs -> CI-OK; bun run check:cursor-parity -> OK
verified.domList: CDP: typing "cats" in the running window produced the engine rows in the DOM (cats, catster, catsolute, catsmile cafe, catster by kingdomoftigers, catsonic livehouse, cats แปลว่า, catsaur) and ArrowDown + Enter opened https://www.google.com/search?q=cats

reference.cursor: this repository's measured Cursor reference covers the right panel as a tab group (Changes, Browser, Terminal, File) and its geometry; nothing captured describes the browser tab's address-bar behaviour, so a suggestion list is not something this work can claim parity with either way
reference.codex: the app this session runs in has an in-app browser for opening pages, and its web search is a tool the agent uses rather than an address-bar completion; that distinction is what this slice follows - Caret's bar completes terms because it is the browser's own address bar

notVerified: Seeing the list with the page behind it: the native view bounds fix was written after that run, and the window could not be relaunched in this environment, so the room it makes is pinned by patch needles and unit tests but was not watched on screen.
The packaged Caret app: it carries the workbench and extension of the run that built it, so it does not have this slice at all - which is the likeliest reason the list was still missing for the user.
Suggestions behind a proxy or offline, and very long terms (the rows ellipsize).
